# ipe() Games

> Four small games from ipe(): Iltonggi, Inkisle, Sunmeld and Claimball. Short rounds, few rules, no ads. None is released yet.

play.ipe.rest is the portal for the games made by ipe() (https://ipe.rest/). It collects four games in one place and links to each game's own official site. None of the four games has been released: no store page or release date exists for any of them. This portal has no accounts, ads or tracking, no journal and no terms of its own (each game's site has its own terms).

## The games

- [Iltonggi](https://iltonggi.ipe.rest): A short, fast, classic territory-conquest strategy game set in Korea's Three Kingdoms era. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iPhone first. Pricing: No ads, no tracking.
- [Inkisle](https://inkisle.ipe.rest): A light island-conquest strategy game for your phone: send fleets between islands and tint the sea your color. Status: In development. Platform: iOS first, Android alongside. Pricing: Every round free · no ads · optional help items.
- [Sunmeld](https://sunmeld.ipe.rest): A merge duel against an AI opponent in one shared tub. Drop a stone, merge matching stones into the next stage, and score. Overflow the tub and you lose. Status: In development. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: Free to try, one purchase unlocks everything, no ads.
- [Claimball](https://claimball.ipe.rest): A casual duel against an AI rival on a notebook grid. The tile where your ball bounces becomes your land. Miss, and you lose land. Status: Coming soon. Platform: iOS and Android. Pricing: No ads. Pricing will be announced closer to launch.

## How ipe makes games

- Short rounds that fit a break: A round should end in minutes, and closing the app should never cost you.
- Few rules, deep reading: If the rules don't fit on one page, the game is asking too much.
- A quiet app: No streak nagging, no ads, no accounts, no tracking.
- Say what's true, including what isn't: If it's not released, we say so. If we haven't checked, we say that too.
- The AI plays fair: Comebacks come from the rules, not from a secretly weakened opponent.
